findings.title: Press_Anchor re-gate drops the chord's swallow reset on ESC frames: same-frame ESC+right+left chord then a non-moved release NO-OPS where the old handle_input click-selected
findings.evidence: OLD (a4d6e9e app/main.odin:536-541 then 545-550): the ESC block latched press_swallowed=true, THEN the chord re-anchor reset it to false — the follow-up non-moved release click-selected. NEW: the map-time re-anchor (mouse.odin:168-169) runs BEFORE the queued Cancel executes (exec.odin:59 latch=true), and the re-gated Press_Anchor is NOT emitted on ESC frames (placing_eff=-1 / esc_cancelled) — the latch sticks true and the executor's Select no-ops. PROBE on b467f9d: [Esc+Right@n1+Left@n1] then [release@n1] leaves sel_node=-1; the old code leaves sel_node=1. Applies to BOTH ESC-chord shapes (±placing).
findings.detail: The r2-W1 fix (suppress the unconditional Press_Anchor) cured the no-ESC drag-interrupt chord but cut the ESC-chord legs with it: r1's unconditional emission matched the old code on ESC frames, the re-gate inverts that. A same-frame ESC+right+left chord is exotic but reachable, and selection state is what the popover/QoS/phase-2 surfaces read — a real mouse-path command/selection delta, the round's ONE hard-blocker category.
findings.recommended_fix: Emit Press_Anchor whenever a same-frame Cancel precedes the chord (has_left && (esc_cancelled || esc_deselect || placing_eff >= 0)), ordered BEFORE Right_Click so the old last-write latch order survives a drag-interrupting right-click (old: ESC-block true -> anchor false -> drag-interrupt true). Pin both ESC-chord legs (±placing) with a chord-then-release scenario asserting the click-select fires.

findings.title: input_parity_esc_release_place ships a MOVED-release shape — the drag_eff leg of the B2 fix is unpinned (deleting `!esc_cancelled` keeps the suite green)
findings.location: harness/parity.odin:697-702 (anchor at chip_router, release at n1) vs app/input/mouse.odin:152

The true r2-B2 shape [press chip, ghost move, board press@n1 while placing, ESC+release@n1] FAILS with the mutation ('sel node 1') and PASSES with the fix — the distinguishing term is `!esc_cancelled` and nothing pins it.

findings.title: esc_pressed is write-only dead state — and always-true anyway (has_key scans zero-initialized [4]Key slots; .Esc is the enum zero value)
findings.evidence: grep: esc_pressed is written twice, read nowhere. `has_key(keys[:], .Esc)` scans all four slots; unwritten slots zero-initialize to .Esc, so the computation is true every frame regardless.
findings.detail: Dead today; a future reader of esc_pressed would silently see always-true.
findings.recommended_fix: Delete esc_pressed (and the has_key call), or scan keys[:keys_n] if a real consumer lands.
